Zerahiah
zer-uh-HYE-uh
proper noun
Hebrew Zerachyah (H2228), the LORD has risen or the LORD shines forth — from zarach (H2224), to rise as the sun, to break forth as light, and Yah, the covenant name.

Biblical Definition

Zerahiah stands in the high-priestly line of Aaron through Eleazar and Phinehas: Uzzi begat Zerahiah, and Zerahiah begat Meraioth (1Ch 6:6), and the genealogy is repeated in the descent of the sons of Aaron (1Ch 6:51). The same line is traced backward in Ezra's own pedigree, where the scribe establishes his right to the priesthood by naming his fathers up to Aaron — the son of Zerahiah, the son of Uzzi, the son of Bukki (Ezr 7:4). A second Zerahiah is the father of Elihoenai, who came up from Babylon with Ezra bringing two hundred males (Ezr 8:4). The name means the LORD has risen, from the verb Scripture uses of the sun coming up over the horizon, and the prophets turn it into a figure for the coming of God to His people: the LORD shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee (Isa 60:2); unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings (Mal 4:2). A priestly house that carried such a name carried a promise it did not live to see fulfilled.

Origin & Era

A priest in the high-priestly line of Aaron through Eleazar, named in Ezra's own pedigree; his name means the LORD has risen.

ZERAHIAH, Hebrew Zerachyah, the LORD has risen, or the LORD shines forth.

1. A priest of the line of Eleazar the son of Aaron; son of Uzzi and father of Meraioth.

He stands in the pedigree by which Ezra proved his descent from Aaron.

2. Father of Elihoenai, who returned from Babylon with Ezra and two hundred males.

From zarach, to rise as the sun or break forth as light.

Key Scripture

1Ch 6:6 — "And Uzzi begat Zerahiah, and Zerahiah begat Meraioth,"

1Ch 6:51 — "Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son,"

Ezr 7:4 — "The son of Zerahiah, the son of Uzzi, the son of Bukki,"

Ezr 8:4 — "Of the sons of Pahathmoab; Elihoenai the son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred males."

Modern Corruption

Genealogies are dismissed as tedious padding; in Ezra's hands one is the legal proof of a right to minister.

expand to see more

The lists of begettings are the most skipped pages in the Bible, and the habit of skipping them costs the reader more than he knows. Ezra 7 shows what a genealogy is for. Before the historian tells us anything Ezra did, he lays out sixteen generations from Ezra back to Aaron the chief priest, because the whole authority of the reformation that follows rests on the man having a right to the office he exercised. The same book records the opposite case: priests who could not find their register were, as polluted, put from the priesthood (Ezr 2:62). Descent was not sentiment; it was law.

The New Testament keeps the principle while changing the register. Office in the church rests on a real call, tested and recognised: no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as was Aaron (Heb 5:4); elders are to be examined against a written standard and appointed with laid-on hands, and let these also first be proved (1Ti 3:10). And the greatest genealogy of all opens the New Testament, because the claim that Jesus is the Christ depends on His descent from David and from Abraham. The principle to recover is that God works through documented, checkable, ordinary succession, and that a church too impatient to read a list will end up too impatient to verify a minister.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Zerachyah (H2228), from zarach (H2224), to rise, to shine forth, with Yah.

expand to see more

Hebrew zarach (H2224) — to rise, to break forth as the sun; the sun ariseth (Ecc 1:5).

Hebrew Zerachyah (H2228) — a priest of Eleazar's line; 1 Chronicles 6:6, 6:51, Ezra 7:4, 8:4.

Hebrew zerach (H2225) — a rising, a dawning; the noun of the same root.

Hebrew yachas (H3187) — to reckon genealogically, to enrol; the machinery of Ezra 2 and 7.

Hebrew shemesh tsedaqah — the Sun of righteousness, who shall arise with healing in his wings (Mal 4:2).

Usage

"“The son of Zerahiah, the son of Uzzi, the son of Bukki” — in Ezra's pedigree."
